tasks.short: Match supplier invoices to purchase orders and goods receipts in AFAS, then book and route for approval.

today.trigger: A supplier invoice arrives by email (PDF) or UBL in the AFAS inbox.
steps: Open the invoice and find the supplier in AFAS
Look up the purchase order and the goods receipt
Compare quantities, prices and VAT line by line
Book the invoice and send it to the budget holder for approval
Chase the buyer or warehouse when lines do not match
drudgery: Searching for the right order number
today.time_sinks: Partial deliveries, price differences and PDFs without an order number take most of the time; clean one-to-one matches are quick but numerous.

lenses.faster: AFAS reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level and posts one-to-one matches with order and receipt itself; the bookkeeper only opens mismatches.
lenses.autonomous: Each arriving invoice is read, matched within set tolerances and released for payment without anyone starting it.
lenses.ambitious: Match every invoice, including the three staffing agencies' invoices against approved hours, instead of spot-checking the large ones.
lenses.joy: No more retyping lines or hunting order numbers; what is left is solving real differences with buyers and suppliers.
lenses.options: Test two or three tolerance settings per supplier group on last quarter's invoices and see touchless rate against error rate before choosing.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the match rules, tolerances and supplier master data, and reviews the weekly touchless rate.

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a price or quantity difference is acceptable, and settling it with the supplier or buyer.
tasks.pattern_why: Matching order, receipt and invoice on structured fields with tolerances is rules on structured data; AFAS does it natively.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice lands in the AFAS scan-and-recognise inbox (UBL or PDF).
steps: AFAS recognises supplier by KvK, VAT number and IBAN and reads lines
System matches lines to purchase order and goods receipt within tolerance
Full matches are booked and approved for payment automatically
Mismatches go to a work queue with the difference highlighted
Bookkeeper resolves, adjusts tolerance or supplier data where the rule was wrong
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper handles every invoice outside tolerance; budget holder approval stays for invoices without a purchase order.
data_needed: Purchase orders and goods receipts in AFAS
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS workflow history per invoice, with match result and who approved exceptions.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level and books and approves one-to-one matches with order or receipt.
AFAS scans a PDF into an e-invoice and finds the supplier by KvK, VAT number and IBAN; gaps are filled by hand.
Escalante Golf went from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds per invoice in NetSuite.
Measured touchless shares often disappoint because of own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions.

risks: Low share of invoices with a purchase order or receipt limits matching
Tolerances set too wide let overcharges through
Supplier master data errors route invoices to the wrong supplier
research_questions: What share of Noordhaven's invoices today has a purchase order and a goods receipt in AFAS?
What touchless rate does AFAS reach on a pilot of one month of real invoices?
How many invoices arrive as UBL versus PDF, per supplier?

tasks.short: Post debits and credits and total accounts in AFAS and Excel sheets, check balances add up.

steps: Enter journal lines in AFAS or prepare them in Excel
Total accounts and subledgers in Excel
Check that totals match AFAS balances
Correct differences and repost
today.time_sinks: Excel side-sheets that duplicate AFAS and must be kept in step by hand.

lenses.faster: Totals and balance checks come straight from AFAS reports or the Power BI extract; the Excel shadow sheets go away.
lenses.autonomous: A nightly check compares subledger totals to the general ledger and flags differences before the morning.
lenses.ambitious: Every account is checked every day, not only at month end, which shortens close.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses adding up columns; the work left is explaining the differences that show up.
lenses.options: Show the check at several cuts (site, administration, cost centre) so the bookkeeper picks where to look.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper defines the control checks and thresholds and keeps them current.
reach: Controller's daily cash and balance view

tasks.human_edge: Deciding which correction is right when a total does not add up.
tasks.pattern_why: Arithmetic and balance checks on structured ledger data are fully rule-based.

steps: Scheduled query totals subledgers and GL accounts
Compares against expected relations and thresholds
Writes differences to an exception list in Power BI or Teams
Bookkeeper corrects the posting in AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: Every correcting entry is posted by a person.
in_practice.logs_to: Exception list history and AFAS journal audit trail.

evidence.claim: Totalling and balance checks on ledger data are standard reporting functions; the Excel arithmetic is replaced by structured data.

risks: Checks built on the nightly extract miss same-day postings
Shadow Excel sheets persist if people do not trust the reports
research_questions: Which Excel sheets do the bookkeepers keep alongside AFAS, and why?
How many balance differences per month are found today, and how late?

tasks.short: Code invoices and other entries to the right ledger account, cost centre and VAT code, and keep records.

today.trigger: Each invoice or entry without a purchase order.
steps: Read the invoice or document
Choose ledger account, cost centre and VAT code
Book in AFAS
Summarise per account for reports
drudgery: Looking up how the same supplier was coded last time
Fixing VAT codes on reverse-charge invoices
today.time_sinks: Invoices without orders and one-off suppliers, where coding takes judgement.

lenses.faster: The system suggests account, cost centre and VAT code from supplier history; the bookkeeper confirms with one click.
lenses.autonomous: Recurring suppliers with stable coding are booked without a person; new or unusual ones wait for review.
lenses.ambitious: Coding becomes consistent enough that cost reports per site and per customer contract can be trusted.
lenses.joy: Less lookup of old bookings; more time on the odd items that need thought.
lenses.options: For a doubtful line, show the top three coding options with how often each was used.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the coding rules and the chart-of-accounts guidance and samples the suggestions.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the right account and VAT treatment for new, mixed or unusual invoices.
tasks.pattern_why: Turning free-text invoice lines into a coding is unstructured-to-structured with a checkable result inside the AFAS flow.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice recognised without an order match.
steps: Model proposes account, cost centre and VAT code with a confidence score
High-confidence recurring suppliers are booked; others are queued
Bookkeeper confirms or corrects
Corrections feed back as supplier coding rules
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper confirms each suggestion below the confidence threshold and all new suppliers.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and VAT code rules
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS booking with suggestion, confidence and confirming user.

evidence.claim: Coding is suggested from vendor history and the team reviews and confirms.
A booking proposal alone is not automation; own accounts and VAT codes block touchless rates.

risks: Wrong VAT code repeated at scale
Intra-EU and reverse-charge invoices need reporting within 5 days once ViDA reporting applies
research_questions: What share of last year's coding corrections by the accountant came from AP bookings?
How accurate are history-based suggestions on a back-test of six months?
How many reverse-charge invoices arrive per month?

tasks.short: Copy totals from side journals, agency portals and Excel sheets into the AFAS general ledger.

today.trigger: Weekly agency hours, monthly accruals and other side records.
steps: Download data from agency portals or Excel
Reformat to the AFAS import layout
Import or type the journal
Check the posted totals
today.time_sinks: Each source has its own format and changes it now and then.

lenses.faster: A fixed import maps each source to the AFAS journal layout; a person only checks the control total.
lenses.autonomous: When an agency portal file or month-end sheet lands, the import runs and posts a draft journal.
lenses.ambitious: Agency hours are booked weekly per site and cost centre, so flex cost is visible before the invoice arrives.
lenses.options: Draft the journal at different levels of detail (per site, per cost centre, per employee group).
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the source-to-ledger mappings and fixes them when a source changes.

tasks.human_edge: Spotting when a source file is wrong or incomplete before it is posted.
tasks.pattern_why: Fixed mappings from structured exports to an import layout; AI coding can build them quickly and they run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: New file in a SharePoint drop folder or portal download.
steps: Script maps the file to the AFAS journal import
Validates control totals and mandatory fields
Posts as draft journal
Bookkeeper releases after a total check
data_needed: Mapping tables to accounts and cost centres
in_practice.logs_to: Import log with file name, control total and releasing user.

evidence.claim: File-to-journal imports with control totals are standard rule-based work.

risks: Silent format change in a portal export
research_questions: Do the three agencies offer a stable export or API of approved hours?
How many manual journals per month come from side sources today?

tasks.short: Reconcile bank, supplier and customer accounts and report differences to the controller.

today.trigger: Daily bank statement and month-end close.
steps: Import Rabobank statement into AFAS
Match open lines by hand where AFAS did not
Reconcile supplier statements
List differences and send them to the controller
drudgery: Hunting for the invoice behind a lump payment
today.time_sinks: Combined payments and missing references from customers.

lenses.faster: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines by reference, IBAN and amount; a model proposes the likely invoices for the unmatched rest with a short explanation.
lenses.autonomous: Unmatched lines get a proposed match and a note every morning without anyone asking.
lenses.ambitious: Supplier statements are reconciled for all main suppliers every month, not just at audit time.
lenses.joy: Less detective work on lump payments; more time fixing the causes with customers.
lenses.options: For each unmatched line, show two or three candidate invoice combinations ranked by fit.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper tunes match rules and tolerances and tracks the unmatched rate.
reach: Credit and collections follow-up of short payments

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what a difference means and who must fix it.
tasks.pattern_why: Rules do most matching; the model only turns unmatched lines and remittance text into a proposed, checkable match.

steps: AFAS rule matching on reference, IBAN, invoice number and amounts
Model reads remittance text and proposes matches for leftovers
Bookkeeper accepts or rejects each proposal
Remaining differences go on a list for the controller
data_needed: Open items per debtor and creditor
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS bank-matching history with proposer and acceptor.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches bank lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and amount; misses go to a person.
Let AP run with people on exceptions and log every decision with its data.

risks: Wrong match closes the wrong customer invoice
Rules tuned too loose hide real differences
research_questions: What share of bank lines does AFAS match today without help?
How long does an unmatched line stay open on average?

tasks.short: Check agency invoices against hours, post the payroll journal and prepare wage and wage-tax payments.

today.trigger: Payroll run (monthly or four-weekly) and weekly agency invoices.
steps: Receive payroll journal from the payroll specialist and post it
Check agency invoices against approved hours
Split the g-rekening share of agency invoices
Prepare net wage and wage-tax payment batches
drudgery: Comparing hours lists line by line
Calculating the g-rekening split by hand
today.time_sinks: Agency invoices with hours that differ from the shift records, in peak season with up to 300 flex workers.

lenses.faster: Agency invoices are checked line by line against approved hours and CAO rates by the system; only differences reach a person.
lenses.autonomous: Each agency invoice triggers the check, the g-rekening split and a draft payment line.
lenses.ambitious: Every flex invoice is checked in full, every week, including rate and allowance rules from the CAO.
lenses.joy: No more ticking hours lists; time goes to settling real disputes with agencies.
lenses.options: Show differences grouped by cause (hours, rate, allowance) so the bookkeeper can choose what to dispute.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the rate tables and check rules with the payroll specialist.

tasks.human_edge: Disputing differences with agencies and deciding what to pay; liability for wage tax stays a judgement.
tasks.pattern_why: Several sources and exceptions (hours, rates, g-rekening, payment) in one flow; a person approves before payment.

in_practice.trigger: Agency invoice or payroll journal arrives.
steps: Agent pulls approved hours and rate tables
Compares invoice lines and flags differences
Calculates g-rekening share per invoice
Prepares payment lines and journal
Bookkeeper reviews differences and approves
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper approves every agency invoice with differences and every payment batch.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS invoice workflow and payment batch history.

evidence.claim: The hirer can be held liable for the agency's unpaid wage tax and VAT and limits this via the g-rekening and record keeping.
Agency invoices checked against time records with only differences to a person is the Noordhaven case in the research.

research_questions: Are approved hours available per flex worker in a structured form?
How large were agency invoice differences last peak season?
Which g-rekening percentages do the three agencies use?

tasks.short: Make sales invoices, customer statements and interest charges from AFAS on schedule.

today.trigger: End of week or month, or completed customer orders.
steps: Collect billable activities (storage, handling, transport)
Create invoices in AFAS
Send statements to customers
Calculate late-payment interest where applied
today.time_sinks: Customer-specific tariffs and surcharges kept in Excel.

lenses.faster: Billable activities flow into AFAS with tariff tables, and invoices and statements go out in one run.
lenses.autonomous: Invoice runs and statements fire on a schedule; only invoices that fail a check stop.
lenses.ambitious: Bill every handling and storage activity, including small surcharges that are missed today, which cuts DSO and leakage.
lenses.joy: No more piecing together billing data; the work is checking odd customers.
lenses.options: Simulate the effect of different invoice frequencies or statement timing on DSO.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns tariff tables and billing rules.

tasks.pattern_why: Tariffs times quantities and statutory interest rules are fully structured.

steps: Pull billable activity
Apply tariff tables
Generate invoices and statements in AFAS
Send e-invoices or PDFs
Exceptions to bookkeeper
in_practice.human_gate: Bookkeeper reviews flagged invoices before sending.

evidence.claim: Billing, interest and account status as deterministic software at autonomy 4.
B2B e-invoicing in the Netherlands planned from 1 July 2030.

risks: Wrong tariff table bills all customers wrong
research_questions: Where is billable activity data kept today?
How much revenue is missed through unbilled surcharges?

tasks.short: Prepare purchase orders and process staff expense claims with receipts.

today.trigger: Request from a department or an expense claim with receipts.
steps: Receive request or claim by email
Create PO in AFAS or check receipts
Check policy and approvals
Book and pay

lenses.faster: Receipts are read automatically and checked against policy; POs are drafted from requests.
lenses.autonomous: Claims within policy go to approval without the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: All purchases get a PO, which raises match rates in AP.
lenses.options: Draft POs with alternative suppliers from history.

tasks.pattern_why: Receipts and free-text requests turn into structured lines with checkable results.

steps: Read receipt or request
Check policy
Draft booking or PO
Route to approver
in_practice.human_gate: Approver signs off each claim; bookkeeper handles exceptions.

evidence.claim: 70% of Dutch respondents approve invoices on paper or by email.

research_questions: How many expense claims and POs per month?
What share of purchases has a PO today?

role.altitude: From keying and matching invoices to owning match rules, tolerances, coding rules and supplier data, and watching the touchless rate and days to close.
reach: Agency invoice checks with the payroll specialist
role.ceiling_note: Limited by data quality: POs, receipts and hours must exist in structure; PDFs, CAO rules and liability decisions keep people in the loop. Perhaps half the role's hours shift to exceptions and rules.
skills_to_grow: Designing match rules and tolerances in AFAS
Data quality and supplier master data
Reading control dashboards in Power BI
role.ambitious_version: A finance back office where nearly all invoices pass without touch, every flex invoice is checked in full, and the bookkeepers run the controls that let the month close in days.
